scenes.heading: Avro Format
scenes.subheading: Row-based format built for data in motion
scenes.narration: Avro is a compact, row-oriented binary format that stores its schema alongside the data, making it ideal for streaming and messaging.

scenes.heading: What makes Avro useful
bullets: Row-oriented, so full records write quickly
scenes.narration: Avro is row-oriented, so writing complete records is fast, which suits streaming ingestion. It stores the schema together with the data, so readers always know how to interpret it. It supports schema evolution gracefully, letting fields be added or changed over time. And its compact binary encoding keeps messages small on the wire.

scenes.heading: Avro vs Parquet
scenes.narration: Avro is row-oriented and shines when writing whole records quickly, as in streaming pipelines. Parquet is columnar and shines when reading a few columns across many rows, as in analytics. Many pipelines land data as Avro on ingestion and later convert it to Parquet for analysis.

scenes.text: Avro is the format of choice for streaming and messaging where fast writes and schema evolution matter.
scenes.narration: The key point is that Avro's fast row writes and strong schema evolution make it the natural fit for streaming and messaging systems.
